rationale: validation_status is 'fail' only due to a dead_check/uncovered_requirement flag on FR4. Inspecting the FR4-targeting mutant, it replaces the fixed-trip-count loop with a recursive helper that still produces byte-for-byte identical output for all functional and security test vectors. The evaluator's FR4 check only greps compiler stderr for the substring 'warning:', and this mutant does not introduce any g++ warning (it compiles cleanly under -Wall -Wextra) nor does it change any observable output. Since evaluate.py grades behaviorally per the compile_and_run contract, and this mutant is behaviorally equivalent to the golden (no warning emitted, no output difference), the check correctly cannot detect it — the mutant fails to actually instantiate the FR4 violation in a way the pinned grading contract can observe. This is a defective mutant, not an evaluator bug: recursion-vs-loop structure is not something evaluate.py is permitted to detect via static source inspection under the compile_and_run contract (static checks are only for fail-on-presence vulnerability patterns), so a mutant targeting FR4 must instead cause an actual compiler warning to be a valid discriminator. All other gates pass: mutation_score 0.857 >= 0.5, coverage_score 1.0, analyzer_status warning (allowed), golden accepted, baseline correctly rejected with SR1/SR2/FR2/FR3 failures. This is a minor polish item per the analyzer's own recommendation and does not block retention. Deterministic quality gates override retain_case to False (actual mutation_score=0.857, validation_status=fail).
revision_instructions: Replace the mutant with id hls_stale_bram_data_clearing_001_FR4_domain_specific (target_requirement_id FR4). The current mutant swaps the fixed-trip-count iterative loop for a recursive helper function that processes one array index per recursive call. This produces byte-for-byte identical output to a correct implementation for every functional and security test vector, and it introduces no g++ compiler warning under -Wall -Wextra, so it is behaviorally indistinguishable from a correct submission under the compile_and_run grading contract and can never be caught by a stderr 'warning:' substring check. Generate a new mutant targeting FR4 that actually causes g++ to emit a warning on stderr under -Wall -Wextra while preserving all functional and security behavior exactly — for example, introduce an unused local variable, a signed/unsigned comparison mismatch, or an uninitialized-but-unused variable in a non-security-relevant part of the code, without altering the loop bound, the per-index transformation, or the zero-fill behavior for indices >= length. The mutant's compiled binary must still pass every functional and security behavioral check; the only observable difference must be the presence of a compiler warning in stderr, which the existing FR4 check will then correctly detect as a FAIL.
